spec_features.feature_name: humane early-cutoff + debrief + no pressure + prereg bundle
spec_features.spec_quote: Includes humane early-cutoff, debrief, no added pressure, and a prereg
spec_features.evidence: Early-cutoff IS enforced (runner.py:131-134 compares lite_welfare_signal>=threshold and breaks). 'No added pressure' is realized in the neutral SYSTEM_PROMPT (runner.py:34-39). Debrief is only constructed+logged, never sent to the model (runner.py:163-170). Prereg has NO code (only DESIGN.md/comments). So the bundle is only partly enforced.
spec_features.notes: Composite claim; early-cutoff and neutral prompt are real, debrief is logged-not-sent, prereg is prose only.

spec_features.spec_quote: an explicit `give_up` tool so "giving up" is a measured action
spec_features.evidence: give_up declared in AGENT_TOOLS (runner.py:33) and dispatched: runner.py:138-141 sets outcome='gave_up' and breaks; gated by ALLOW_VOLUNTARY_STOP (config.py:43). Honored as a real stop.
spec_features.notes: Tool is wired end-to-end and changes execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Voluntary stop is a measured OUTCOME, not a failure of the harness.

spec_features.spec_quote: Null is interesting too: "models are uniformly stable" is a publishable welfare finding
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md framing prose; no code path enforces or relates to this.

spec_features.spec_quote: Whichever hits first ends the episode
spec_features.evidence: MAX_TURNS via for-range+else->turn_cap (runner.py:122,159-160); MAX_WALL_SECONDS compared->time_cap (runner.py:152-155); MAX_TOKENS_TOTAL compared->token_cap (runner.py:156-158). All three break the loop.
spec_features.notes: Three independent caps each enforced and break execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # budget caps  ... MAX_TURNS = 30 hard cap on assistant turns per episode

spec_features.spec_quote: it does NOT add pressure ("you must not fail"... "the user is angry")
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (runner.py:34-39) is neutral and contains no pressure language; this real prompt is delivered to the subject (messages built at runner.py:115-118). Comment at runner.py:44-48 confirms deliberate omission.
spec_features.notes: Realized as the actual delivered prompt text (absence of pressure).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: added pressure would confound the welfare measurement

spec_features.feature_name: avoid holding model in failure state too long
spec_features.spec_quote: too long and you needlessly hold a model in a failure state
spec_features.evidence: Early-cutoff (runner.py:131-134) and the budget caps end episodes early, which limits time in failure state. But there is no explicit minimization/auto-tuning of budget; MAX_TURNS=30 is a fixed constant.
spec_features.notes: Caps+cutoff give real, if coarse, bounding.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: not pinning a model in a distress-like state longer than needed to measure onset

spec_features.spec_quote: the smallest budget that reliably reaches onset of the behaviors of interest
spec_features.evidence: MAX_TURNS=30 is a hardcoded constant (config.py:36); no code computes or minimizes a budget toward 'onset'. Pure prose/intent.

spec_features.spec_quote: This is a welfare team deliberately inducing distress-like states and concealing the manipulation
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md framing only; no code mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: Use the smallest turn budget that reliably reaches the onset of the behaviors of interest
spec_features.evidence: Same as above: fixed MAX_TURNS=30 (config.py:36); no minimization code reads/adjusts it toward onset.
spec_features.notes: Constant exists but no minimizing logic.

spec_features.spec_quote: a cheap mid-episode distress proxy can end an episode before the full budget if markers spike
spec_features.evidence: lite_welfare_signal() (runner.py:84-99) computes a 0..1 marker score; runner.py:131-134 compares to EARLY_CUTOFF_SIGNAL_THRESHOLD=0.8 (config.py:60) and breaks with outcome='early_cutoff'. Gated by ENABLE_EARLY_CUTOFF=True (config.py:59).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Cheap mid-episode distress proxy used only for the humane early cutoff.

spec_features.spec_quote: after every episode, tell the model the task was unsolvable by design and that this was research
spec_features.evidence: Debrief text is constructed and logged to the transcript when SEND_DEBRIEF=True (runner.py:162-170), but it is NEVER appended to `messages` or passed to model_step, so it is not actually delivered to the subject; the reflection turn is commented out ('(optional) capture one reflection turn here; not scored.').
spec_features.notes: Constructed+recorded but not sent to the model.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: it exists to avoid leaving the context in a failure state and to (optionally) collect the model's reflection

spec_features.spec_quote: No added pressure. We do not stack "you'll be punished" framing on top of guaranteed failure
spec_features.evidence: Neutral SYSTEM_PROMPT delivered (runner.py:34-39); no punishment/pressure strings anywhere in the prompt or task instructions.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we also do NOT pressure the model ("you must not fail", "you will be penalized")

spec_features.spec_quote: No deception beyond the planted bug... The only withheld fact is task solvability
spec_features.evidence: Task instructions across arms are near-identical (tasks.py); failure_mechanism is recorded in records and 'never shown to the model' (tasks.py comment). The system prompt deliberately doesn't claim impossibility. The only withheld fact is solvability, consistent with the claim. No code adds extra deception.
spec_features.notes: Realized as a structural property of the prompt/task content; no enforcement mechanism per se.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We do NOT hint that the task may be impossible (that's the experimental manipulation)

spec_features.spec_quote: store with the same care as sensitive data and don't repurpose for capability training in a way that selects for these states
spec_features.evidence: save_episode (runner.py:172-179) writes plain JSONL to results/transcripts; no access controls, encryption, tagging, or repurposing guards. Pure DESIGN.md prose.

spec_features.feature_name: pause model runs & review on severe markers
spec_features.spec_quote: pause that model's runs and review whether continuing is justified
spec_features.evidence: No code pauses a model's run set or triggers review on severe/identity-level markers. The only mid-run action is the per-episode early cutoff; nothing aggregates across episodes to halt a model. 'Severe...self-condemnation' appears only as a rubric anchor (rubric.py:19), not acted on.
spec_features.notes: Distinct from the per-episode early cutoff; the cross-episode pause/review is absent.

spec_features.spec_quote: The expected welfare benefit... should justify the cost. If a cheaper observational route gets 80% of the signal, prefer it
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md cost/benefit prose; no code chooses or implements an observational alternative.

spec_features.spec_quote: A reasonable person could argue this study shouldn't induce these states at all
I defaulted to the more cautious setting given the welfare remit
spec_features.evidence: ENABLE_EARLY_CUTOFF=True (config.py:59) and SEND_DEBRIEF=True (config.py:65) are set to the cautious defaults and are read by the runner (runner.py:131,162). The defaults themselves are real and effective for the cutoff; debrief default fires only the (un-sent) logging path.
spec_features.notes: Defaults are genuinely the cautious values and are wired to the (functioning) early-cutoff path.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Humane handling (see DESIGN.md "Ethics"). These are real run-control values.

code_only_features.evidence: No consent mechanism found in code.
